note: Adapted from Emerson's (1928) description of the species, originally in English; the soldier is divided into two size forms, listed separately as in the original; alates and nymphs were not described in the original. Figure numbers, localities and host records have been deleted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Body slightly smaller than in A. latinotus. Compared with the syntypes of A. guineensis, the sides of the head are straighter, the apical curvature of the mandibles stronger and the anterior pronotal margin more deeply concave; the latter is larger. The concave margin of the pronotum is less deep than shown in the figure of var. guineensis.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head surface sparsely covered with setae; antennae 14–15-segmented, in the 14-segmented condition the third segment slightly longer than the second and the fourth slightly shorter than the second, in the 15-segmented condition the third segment shorter than the fourth and the fourth shorter than the second; apices of the mandibles strongly incurved; anterior margin of the pronotum deeply concave. Measurements: head length 1.89, head width 1.10–1.20, pronotum median length 0.50, total length 0.60, width 0.72–0.78, hind tibia 0.97–1.05, left mandible 0.80. Minor soldier: antennae 14-segmented; head length 1.44, head width 0.78, pronotum median length 0.33, width 0.58, hind tibia 0.83, left mandible 0.67. The worker is recorded in the original only as having 15-segmented antennae.
